description: coFlipper command catalog, on two layers. 'device' = CFP commands sent over the serial port to the Flipper ('cfp <id> <name> [arguments]', see /PROTOCOL.md), executed directly by the hardware. 'agent' = high-level operations, executed on the desktop, which combine one or more device commands with LLM (Gemini) reasoning - this is the original part of the project, not the device commands taken individually, which replicate functions already present in the Flipper Zero firmware. Commands with 'agent_visible': false are for internal use and are not exposed to the model as callable tools.

commands.name: ping
commands.description: Checks whether the CFP server on the Flipper responds.

commands.name: info
commands.description: The name/model of the connected Flipper device.

commands.name: device.battery
commands.description: The current battery level and whether it is charging.

commands.name: device.storage.list
commands.description: Lists the files saved on the SD card in a given folder (saved IR/Sub-GHz signals, saved NFC cards, etc.).

args.name: path
args.description: path on the SD card, e.g. /ext/subghz

commands.name: exit
commands.description: Closes the CFP application on the Flipper, remotely. Needed during development: reinstalling the application requires the previous instance to be closed, and without this command the Back button would have to be pressed physically on every iteration.

commands.name: subghz.rssi
commands.description: Measures the signal level (RSSI, in dBm) on a given frequency, listening for approximately 100 ms. Values close to -50 dBm indicate a strong signal, those below -90 dBm generally indicate only background noise. It does not decode the signal, only quantifies its presence.
commands.returns: the frequency actually synthesized by the radio (Hz) and the peak RSSI value (dBm)

commands.name: subghz.scan
commands.description: Scans a list of known frequencies and reports on which of them activity is detected (RSSI above a threshold).
commands.returns: a list of frequencies with a detected signal

commands.name: subghz.read
commands.description: Listens on a specific frequency and tries to identify the protocol of the captured signal (e.g. a gate remote, a weather station).

args.name: timeout_ms
args.description: how long it waits for a signal, 5000 by default

commands.returns: the detected protocol (if known), the raw captured data

commands.name: subghz.replay
commands.description: Retransmits a Sub-GHz signal previously saved on the SD card. Intended for testing one's own devices (e.g. one's own gate remote), not for someone else's signals.

commands.name: ir.read
commands.description: Waits for and decodes the next IR signal received (e.g. a button press on a remote pointed at the Flipper).

args.name: timeout_ms
args.description: how long it waits for a signal, 5000 by default

commands.returns: the decoded protocol, address, and command

commands.name: ir.learn
commands.description: Learns a new IR signal (from a physical remote) and saves it under a given name, for later reuse.

args.name: name
args.description: the name to save the signal under, e.g. tv_power

commands.name: ir.send
commands.description: Retransmits a previously saved IR signal (universal remote functionality).

args.name: name
args.description: the name of the saved signal, e.g. tv_power

commands.name: nfc.read
commands.description: Waits for an NFC tag/card brought close to the Flipper and returns its UID and type.

args.name: timeout_ms
args.description: how long it waits for a card, 5000 by default

commands.name: nfc.watch
commands.description: Monitors, over a period of time, all NFC tags/cards that come within range of the module.
commands.returns: a list of detected card UIDs/types, in chronological order, with timestamps

commands.name: nfc.emulate
commands.description: Emulates a previously saved NFC card (the Flipper behaves like that card towards a reader).

args.name: name
args.description: the name of the saved card

commands.name: rfid.read
commands.description: Reads a low-frequency RFID card (125 kHz) brought close to the Flipper.

args.name: timeout_ms
args.description: how long it waits for a card, 5000 by default

commands.name: agent.check_frequency_activity
commands.description: Interprets in natural language the signal level measured on one or more frequencies: it translates the raw dBm values into a useful conclusion ('on 433.92 MHz there is clear activity, on 868 MHz only background noise'), correlates the frequency with its typical uses and, on request, compares several frequencies to indicate where it is worth listening. It relies exclusively on real measurements obtained through subghz.rssi.

args.name: frequency
args.description: the frequency of interest; if absent, the agent picks the common ISM frequencies

commands.returns: a natural-language interpretation of the measured signal levels

commands.name: agent.explain_subghz_capture
commands.description: Translates the raw result of a Sub-GHz capture into natural language: what type of device is likely the source of the signal (gate/car remote, sensor, weather station, etc.), based on the frequency, the detected protocol, and a purpose-built database of frequency-protocol-device correspondences, rather than just displaying the raw code as the stock Flipper application does.

args.name: frequency
args.description: the frequency to probe, in Hz

commands.returns: a natural-language explanation + the confidence level of the identification

commands.name: agent.nfc_session_summary
commands.description: Runs nfc.watch for the specified duration and builds a natural-language summary of the session: how many distinct cards/tags were seen, which one repeated, and a guess about the usage context (e.g. 'it looks like the phone interacted 3 times with the same reader, possibly a transit pass'). This answers exactly the project's initial idea: to show what a phone's NFC connected with.

args.name: duration_ms
args.description: the duration of the monitoring session

commands.returns: a text summary + a structured list of the events

commands.name: agent.identify_ir_device
commands.description: Captures an unknown IR signal and tries to deduce what type of appliance/brand emitted it, based on the timing fingerprint of the protocol (NEC, RC5, Samsung, etc.), also offering an explanation of the reasoning, not just the protocol label.
commands.returns: a guess about the type/brand of the appliance + the decoded protocol

commands.name: agent.confirm_authorized_action
commands.description: A mandatory safety gate before any device command that transmits/acts upon the real world (subghz.replay, nfc.emulate, ir.send): the agent explicitly asks the user to confirm that they are acting on their own device, before sending the command to the Flipper. It executes nothing by itself, it only validates the intent.

args.name: action
args.description: the name of the device command about to be sent

commands.returns: confirmation or refusal, with the reason
